title: UL kinematics (spatial shape gradients and current Jacobian)
objective: Implement Updated-Lagrangian kinematics in the symbolic layer: the current-configuration Jacobian j = sum_a (dN_a/dxi) x_ai and the spatial shape-function gradients dN_a/dx_i = (dN_a/dxi_j) j^{-1}_{ji}, so the UL residual emitter (P1-3) can integrate over the deformed configuration.

plan_assets.asset_description: B1.1 residual integrand (defines Jacobian with respect to current coordinates and spatial shape gradient formula).

scope: Add `current_jacobian` and `spatial_shape_gradient` helpers alongside the existing reference-configuration helpers in `mechdsl.symbolic.kinematics` and `mechdsl.lib.tensor_ops`.
Store the computed j and dN/dx on `ElementIR` under CURRENT configuration slots (populated only when `ConfigurationIR.configuration == CURRENT`).
Cover: single element at identity (j = J0, dN/dx = dN/dX), at known simple shear, and at known rigid rotation (j = R @ J0, dN/dx transforms correctly).
implementation_steps: Add `current_jacobian(dN_dxi, x_elem)` returning j = x_elem.T @ dN_dxi.
Add `spatial_shape_gradient(dN_dxi, j)` returning dN/dx = dN_dxi @ inv(j).
Wire the helpers into `ElementIR` population: when the IR `configuration` is CURRENT, populate `geometry.j_current` and `geometry.spatial_shape_gradients`.
Add symbolic-layer tests verifying identity, pure shear, and pure rotation.
Run fast suite to confirm no regressions.
acceptance_criteria: For `F = I`, j equals the reference Jacobian J0 at every quadrature point.
For a known simple-shear deformation, j matches the hand calculation.
For a rigid body rotation, the spatial shape gradients satisfy dN/dx = R @ (dN/dX).
No regressions in the 998 existing fast tests.
verification_commands: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu' -q
risks: inv(j) is undefined when det(j) <= 0. Mitigation: add a positive-determinant guard with the same tolerance as the existing J0 guard (1e-15).
Python-level operations may diverge slightly from the generator's Taichi implementation. Mitigation: keep the helpers numpy-only and let P1-3 mirror the exact same closed form.

commands.command: uv run pytest packages/mechdsl-core/tests/ -m 'not slow and not gpu'

completion_notes: Added current_jacobian(dN_dxi, x_elem) and spatial_shape_gradient(dN_dxi, j) as Mat33 primitives in mechdsl/lib/tensor_ops.py — shape-generic NumPy helpers, sit alongside deformation_gradient/det_33/inv_33.

Added current_gradient_at_physical(X_elem, x_elem, q) in mechdsl/codegen/hex8_tables.py as the per-QP mirror of reference_gradient_at_physical. Returns (dN/dx, det(j)) with a non-positive-determinant guard carrying an element-inversion diagnostic. X_elem is kept in the signature for API symmetry so P1-4 can compute both J0 and j in a single call when it emits the Jaumann-material + geometric-stiffness two-term tangent.

Interpretive deviation (Gate B, acknowledged): scope called for storing j and dN/dx on ElementIR under CURRENT geometry slots. The existing codebase computes the reference counterpart on-demand via reference_gradient_at_physical — ElementIR stores no J0 slot either. Adding UL-only storage slots would create an asymmetric design. Followed the existing on-demand pattern; the per-QP helper is the on-demand equivalent of the storage slot. The 4th test case was rewritten accordingly to assert the helper's shape/contract.

Minor (Gate B m1): current_gradient_at_physical keeps X_elem in the signature for P1-4 API symmetry but currently del's it. Low-impact — removing later is strictly cheaper than re-adding. Flagged for P1-4 implementer to verify actual consumption.
